findings.title: Hung spawn process is never killed on restart
findings.description:
The old `_ensure_process_alive` called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. The new code guards it with `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process):`. Production processes come from `self.mp_context.Process` (flusher.py:105), which is a `SpawnProcess`. In both CPython 3.12 and 3.13, `SpawnProcess` subclasses `process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.context.Process` (`context.py:220` vs `context.py:284`/`332`), so the guard is always False and `kill()` never runs.

Impact: on the `hang` cause (process alive, `healthy_since` stale), the code bumps the restart counter and starts a replacement with `_create_process_for_shards`, but the hung process keeps running on the same `span-buf:q:*` queues. Orphans can accumulate up to `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` per index, and if the hung process resumes it can flush the same queues as its replacement, which risks duplicate segments on `buffered-segments`. The `no_process` path is unaffected because the process is already dead. The `AttributeError` in the `except` clause is also unreachable.

Fix: kill any non-thread process, e.g. `if not isinstance(process, threading.Thread): process.kill()`. No test covers this path (see the test-debt finding below).

findings.title: `join()` never terminates spawn processes, and a deadline break skips the rest
findings.description:
The `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard at line 346 has the same flaw, so `terminate()` never runs for production processes. The original single-process `join` had this same bug, so it is pre-existing, but the diff now copies it across every process. Separately, when the deadline passes, the loop `break`s at line 341 and never terminates the remaining processes. Once the guard is fixed, that break will leave them running.

Fix: use the `threading.Thread` check and terminate every process whether or not the deadline has passed.

findings.title: Per-process buffers repeat Redis memory queries and double-count the same cluster
findings.description:
`submit()` now calls `get_memory_info()` on every entry in `self.buffers`. Each per-process `SpansBuffer` resolves to the same `settings.SENTRY_SPAN_BUFFER_CLUSTER` (`buffer.py:117-118`, `161-163`). `get_memory_info` calls `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` (`buffer.py:375-376`, `memory.py:82-105`), which runs a cluster-wide `INFO` on every call. With P processes that is P cluster-wide `INFO` calls per submit, and each master's memory is added P times to `used` and `available`.

The ratio check comes out correct only because every copy is identical, so the threshold holds by accident while the summed values are wrong. Query memory once instead of once per process.

findings.title: `max-flush-segments` is now a per-process budget, so peak memory scales with `flusher_processes`
findings.description:
`flush_segments` derives `shard_factor` from `len(self.assigned_shards)` of the buffer it runs on. Each flusher process now holds only its own k shards, so each one uses `ceil(max_flush_segments / k)` per shard and can load about `max_flush_segments` segments per cycle. Before this change, the total across the consumer was about `max_flush_segments`. `_load_segment_data` (`buffer.py:458-521`) loads all selected segments into memory at once, so peak memory now grows roughly with `flusher_processes`. The option's meaning also changes for P > 1 with no documentation.

Fix: split the budget across processes, or document the new semantics explicitly.

findings.title: Dead code and an always-true guard
findings.description: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is never called anywhere in `src/` or `tests/`. The `if not process: continue` guard at lines 222-223 is always False, because neither `multiprocessing` process objects nor `threading.Thread` define `__bool__` or `__len__`. Remove both. The guard hides the fact that `self.processes` is always populated.

findings.title: Docstring and CLI default disagree; factory and CLI defaults differ
findings.description:
The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard." The CLI option defaults to `1` (`src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:432-437`), which means one process for all shards. The factory defaults `flusher_processes` to `None` (`factory.py:41`), which gives one process per shard via `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` (`flusher.py:51`). The same knob has two defaults, and the docstring describes only one of them.

Fix: pick a single default, set it in one place, and document the actual behavior.

findings.title: Negative `--flusher-processes` crashes the consumer at construction
findings.description:
The CLI option is `type=int` with no lower bound. For -1, `max_processes` is truthy, `num_processes = min(-1, n) = -1`, and `process_to_shards_map` becomes `{}`. Then `i % -1` evaluates to `0`, and `self.process_to_shards_map[0]` raises `KeyError` on the first shard. Zero is absorbed by the `or` fallback.

Fix: `click.Option(..., type=click.IntRange(min=1))` in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:432-437`, and optionally a guard in `SpanFlusher.__init__`.

findings.title: The added `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` is a no-op
findings.description:
The test begins with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` (line 15). That replaces `time.sleep` on the shared `time` module, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added at line 62 does nothing. The flusher threads are not synchronized with the drift change, and `step.join()` sets `stopped`, which can end the loop before a flush happens. The assertion `(msg,) = messages` can therefore fail intermittently. The comment "Give flusher threads time" is misleading.

Fix: wait on the observable result (poll `messages` against a deadline captured with the real clock) instead of sleeping.

findings.title: No behavioral test for restart/kill or shard distribution
findings.description:
`test_flusher_processes_limit` checks internal structures (`len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.num_processes`, sums over `process_to_shards_map`). It does not check which shards land on which process (for 4 shards and 2 processes, the expected mapping is {0: [0, 2], 1: [1, 3]}), does not flush or produce any segment through the multi-process path, and does not exercise `_ensure_processes_alive`, which is the path the FAIL finding is about.

Fix: add a test that simulates a dead or hung process and asserts that the old process is killed and a replacement is started, and assert observable output rather than internal attributes.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tags and overlapping attribute names
findings.description: The same concept is tagged three different ways. `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `shard` with a comma-joined list of the process's shards (lines 185, 192-196). `wait_produce` uses `shards` (line 199). `flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard` with a single integer (lines 243-245). Pick one key and one value shape so dashboards can aggregate them. Separately, `SpanFlusher.num_processes` (flusher process count) and `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.num_processes` (batch pool size) share a name for different things; rename one.
